newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Opposition newspaper folds in Colombia.
newsitem.headline: Opposition newspaper folds in Colombia.

text.p: Colombia's opposition newspaper La Prensa, known for feisty headlines and attacks on President Ernesto Samper, hit newsstands for the last day on Friday.

The muckraking Bogota tabloid, whose leading shareholders included former president Misael Pastrana, was founded nine years ago and finally succumbed to financial pressures stemming from a steady loss of advertising.
"The freest newspaper in the world is shutting down," La Prensa's directors said in one of several editorials announcing that Friday's edition would be its last.

"It was an idea that began nine years ago, that endured and fought the corruption of (former president Cesar) Gaviria and revealed the ties between Ernesto Samper Pizano and his administration friends with drug trafficking."
Gaviria, now secretary-general of the Organization of American States, is a member of Samper's ruling Liberal Party. The Pastrana family has dominated its arch-rival Conservative Party for decades.

La Prensa was one of the most aggressive trackers of the scandal that erupted shortly before Samper took office in August 1994, when it was first alleged that he used millions of dollars in drug money to finance his campaign.

But its reporting was often dismissed as slanted since Misael Pastrana's son, Andres, finished a close second to Samper in the 1994 elections and his other son, Juan Carlos, was the daily's publisher.
